pos.personaBrief: Jairo dos Santos describes an 'extremamente ofensivo' side whose average positions looked like a 2-3-5, and the midfield four 'knew what to do with the ball' (Falcao via FIFA): Brazil dominated by having the ball and attacking with it, never by ceding it.

pro.personaBrief: The midfield 'passed with invention' and Telê wanted midfielders who knew what to do with the ball (FIFA), with Falcao and Cerezo as the two playmakers (ESPN); progression came through combination play rather than direct long balls, though a static target Serginho was kept up front.

est.personaBrief: Falcao: Telê 'wanted us to play intuitively and not systematically'; the midfield rotated so as not to give reference points (Trellini), Zico, Socrates and Falcao took turns on the right (Trivela), and Telê said fixed wingers 'ja estao mortos', a clearly relational structure, even though Serginho stayed as a static centre-forward.

lar.personaBrief: Telê dropped the right winger for a fourth central midfielder (Trellini: the right wing 'deve se tornar cada vez mais um espaco vazio'), there were practically no Brazilian moves down the right flank v Italy (Trivela), and width came from Eder on the left and the attacking full-backs; the best players were concentrated in the centre.

blo.personaBrief: After losing the ball Brazil tried to win it back at once (Trivela) and the whole team pushed forward even at 2-2 (ESPN), but Zico and Socrates 'couldn't drop back' and Serginho was a static forward, so the press was immediate rather than an organised high press led by the forwards.

mar.personaBrief: No source says whether Brazil marked zonally or man-to-man (openQuestions); Zico's rule 'Whoever was closer to the ball had to close down' points to a space-based logic, and unlike Bearzot (Gentile on Zico) Telê assigned no man-markers, so the answers lean zonal by inference.

pla.personaBrief: Brazil kept attacking at 2-2 against Italy when a draw would have been enough (ESPN, Jornal de Brasilia), Telê imposed his no-fixed-winger idea with Zico playing on the right 'a contragosto' (Trellini), and he reportedly brushed off warnings about Italy; at half-time against the USSR he took risks but kept the attacking plan.

res.personaBrief: Telê: 'Quem gosta de futebol gosta de ver aquele futebol de 82' (1992); the team kept attacking when a draw was enough against Italy, but his primary statements reject choosing beauty over winning, so how you win matters without being a choice between the two.

sis.personaBrief: Telê fitted four creators together and asked them to play 'intuitively and not systematically' (Falcao); Zico and Socrates were spared defensive work while Falcao and Cerezo covered (Zico, The Blizzard): talent decided, and the system served it.

jog.personaBrief: Even the holding pair were playmakers (Falcao and Cerezo, ESPN), and the squad was picked for technique, with midfielders 'who knew what to do with the ball' (FIFA); the creators did not drop back and still played, so technique clearly beats physicality.

bas.personaBrief: The core was experienced (Zico 29, Socrates/Falcao 28, others 27), but Telê gave the young Leandro the right-back place over Edevaldo and made the 21-year-old Careca first-choice striker; as a national team it was built from the best players anywhere, overseas-based included (FIFA).

lid.personaBrief: No verified evidence for this axis; from general knowledge Telê was a strict, demanding disciplinarian (described as 'stubbornly strict', Game of the People), consistent with his insistence on full autonomy over call-ups (context, 1980): authority over harmony.
